title: Extraction of High-Quality RNA from Auxenochlorella protothecoides
author: Dimitrios J. Camacho
materials: Return the standards to the 4 °C referigerator.

Allow all reagents to equilibrate at room temperature for at least 30 min. Protect all solutions from light. Keep samples on wet ice. While reagents equilibrate to room temperature, follow steps 37 and 38 to dilute and denature RNA samples.
Once all reagents are equilibrated to room temperature, vortex the RNA dye concentrate for 10 s and centrifuge for 30 s, 16,000 × g at room temperature.

steps.title: Harvest cells
steps.instruction: Transfer the required volume of Auxenochlorella protothecoides culture to a 15 mL high‑speed centrifuge tube, centrifuge 2 min at 10 000 × g, room temperature, and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Calculate cell volume
steps.instruction: Determine cell density with a hemocytometer (see Camacho & Merchant, 2024) and calculate the culture volume needed to collect 1–3 × 10⁸ cells.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet in shield
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in 750 µL DNA/RNA Shield solution by pipetting up and down, then transfer the suspension to a ZR BashingBead Lysis Tube (0.1 µm & 0.5 µm beads) and cap tightly.

steps.title: Bead‑beating lysis
steps.instruction: Lyse the cells in a Biospec Mini Bead Beater 16 for 3 min 30 s in a 4 °C cold room, then repeat for a total of 7 min.

steps.title: Centrifuge lysate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysate 30 s at 16 000 × g, room temperature, and transfer 400 µL of the supernatant into a new nuclease‑free 1.5 mL tube.

steps.title: Load Zymo‑Spin IICG column – part 1
steps.instruction: Place a green Zymo‑Spin IICG column into a collection tube, add 750 µL of the lysate mixture, centrifuge 30 s at 16 000 × g, room temperature, discard flow‑through, and repeat until all lysate from the previous step has passed through the column.

steps.title: Add RNA Prep Buffer – round 1
steps.instruction: Add 400 µL RNA Prep Buffer to the column, centrifuge 30 s at 16 000 × g, room temperature, and discard the flow‑through.

steps.title: Load Zymo‑Spin IICG column – part 2
steps.instruction: Place a green Zymo‑Spin IICG column into a collection tube, transfer the remaining mixture (from step 7) into the column, centrifuge 30 s at 16 000 × g, room temperature, discard flow‑through, and repeat until all mixture has been processed.

steps.title: Add RNA Prep Buffer – round 2
steps.instruction: Add 400 µL RNA Prep Buffer to the column, centrifuge 30 s at 16 000 × g, room temperature, and discard the flow‑through.

steps.title: Transfer eluate to Zymo‑Spin III‑HRC
steps.instruction: Transfer the eluted RNA from the previous column into a prepared Zymo‑Spin III‑HRC filter placed in a 1.5 mL tube and centrifuge 3 min at 16 000 × g, room temperature.

steps.title: Prep Zymo‑Spin III‑HRC filter
steps.instruction: Place a fresh Zymo‑Spin III‑HRC filter into a new collection tube, add 600 µL ZymoBIOMICS Prep Solution (different from RNA Prep Buffer), centrifuge 3 min at 8 000 × g, room temperature, discard flow‑through and collection tube, then transfer the filter into a new 1.5 mL tube.

steps.title: First RNA wash
steps.instruction: Add 700 µL RNA Wash Buffer to the column, centrifuge 30 s at 16 000 × g, room temperature, and discard the flow‑through.

steps.title: Second RNA wash
steps.instruction: Add 400 µL RNA Wash Buffer to the column, centrifuge 30 s at 16 000 × g, room temperature, discard the flow‑through, then centrifuge again 30 s at 16 000 × g to remove residual liquid, and transfer the column to a new nuclease‑free 1.5 mL tube.

steps.title: Add ethanol to wash buffer
steps.instruction: Verify that ethanol has been added to the RNA Wash Buffer, then add 400 µL RNA Wash Buffer to the column, centrifuge 30 s at 16 000 × g, discard flow‑through, centrifuge another 30 s at 16 000 × g to remove residual liquid, and transfer the column to a new nuclease‑free 1.5 mL tube.

steps.title: Add ethanol – step A
steps.instruction: Add 300 µL of 100 % ethanol to the sample and mix.

steps.title: Add ethanol – step B
steps.instruction: Add 800 µL of 100 % ethanol to the sample and mix.

steps.title: Add RNA Lysis Buffer – step A
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL RNA Lysis Buffer to the sample and mix.

steps.title: Add RNA Lysis Buffer – step B
steps.instruction: Add 400 µL RNA Lysis Buffer to the supernatant and mix.

steps.title: Elute RNA – first elution
steps.instruction: Add 85 µL RNase‑free water directly to the centre of the column matrix (do not add water to the tube walls), incubate 1 min at room temperature, centrifuge 30 s at 16 000 × g, room temperature, collect eluate.

substeps.instruction: Optional second elution: add an additional 85 µL RNase‑free water to the centre of the column matrix, incubate 1 min at room temperature, centrifuge 30 s at 16 000 × g, room temperature, collect eluate, determine its concentration with a NanoDrop, and discard the column.

steps.title: Elute RNA – variable volume
steps.instruction: Add 50–100 µL RNase‑free water directly to the centre of the column matrix (do not add water to the tube walls), incubate 1 min at room temperature, centrifuge 30 s at 16 000 × g, room temperature, collect eluate.

substeps.instruction: Optional second elution: add an additional 50–100 µL RNase‑free water to the centre of the column matrix, incubate 1 min at room temperature, centrifuge 30 s at 16 000 × g, room temperature, collect eluate, determine its concentration with a NanoDrop, and discard the column.

steps.title: Flash‑freeze RNA
steps.instruction: Flash‑freeze the purified RNA samples (not QC aliquots) in liquid nitrogen and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Aliquot RNA for QC
steps.instruction: Aliquot 5 µL of purified RNA into a new 1.5 mL tube for QC: use 1.5 µL for NanoDrop (A230/A260 and A280/A260 ratios), 1 µL for Qubit fluorescence quantification, 1 µL for Bioanalyzer quality assessment, and reserve 1.5 µL for pipette error or re‑measurement. Keep the QC tube on wet ice.

steps.title: Measure RNA with NanoDrop
steps.instruction: Measure RNA concentration and A260/A230, A260/A280 ratios using a NanoDrop (use 1.5 µL sample and 1.5 µL blank). Typical RNA from 10⁸ cells is 150–400 ng/µL; pure RNA shows A260/A280 ≈ 2.1 and A260/A230 > 2.0.

steps.title: Prepare Qubit assay
steps.instruction: Bring Qubit Broad Range standards #1 and #2 to room temperature, protect all solutions from light, and also bring Bioanalyzer reagents to room temperature if they will be used immediately.

steps.title: Make Qubit working solution
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1:200 working solution of RNA BR Reagent in RNA BR Buffer (10 µL reagent + 1990 µL buffer). For each sample you will need 199 µL working solution + 1 µL RNA; for each standard you need 190 µL working solution + 10 µL standard. For 4 samples (2 replicates each) plus 2 standards, make 2 mL working solution (10 reactions). Mix the working solution in a nuclease‑free plastic container, protect from light.

steps.title: Load Qubit tubes
steps.instruction: For each sample, add 199 µL working solution and 1 µL RNA to a thin‑wall, clear 0.5 mL Qubit assay tube. For each standard, add 190 µL working solution and 10 µL standard. Invert tubes to mix, centrifuge briefly to collect liquid at the bottom, and incubate upright in the dark at room temperature for 2 min (stable up to 3 h).

steps.title: Power on Qubit
steps.instruction: Plug the Qubit instrument into an outlet (the Qubit 4 has no power button).

steps.title: Set Qubit method
steps.instruction: On the Home screen select “RNA”, then “RNA Broad Range”, then “Read Standards”.

steps.title: Read standards
steps.instruction: Wipe the sides of all tubes with a clean Kimwipe, insert Standard #1 tube, close the lid, select “Read standard”, record the fluorescence (RFU). Repeat for Standard #2.

steps.title: Label Qubit tubes
steps.instruction: Pour enough 0.5 mL Qubit assay tubes for all samples (including replicates) and two additional tubes for standards, label the lids only (do not label tube sides).

steps.title: Run Qubit samples
steps.instruction: Select “Run samples”, input 1 µL for Sample Volume and choose ng/µL as unit. Insert each tube, read, and record the concentration. If a sample reads “Out of Range”, record the raw RFU, plot the standard curve (RFU vs concentration), calculate the required dilution factor, dilute the RNA in water, remake the reaction with new standards, and re‑measure.

steps.title: Denature RNA for Bioanalyzer
steps.instruction: Denature the diluted RNA samples at 70 °C for 2 min (RNA ladder need not be denatured if already done).

steps.title: Prepare gel‑dye mix
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL RNA dye concentrate to 65 µL filtered gel, vortex 5 s, centrifuge 10 min at 13 000 × g, room temperature. Use the prepared gel within one day; one 65 µL aliquot suffices for two chips.

steps.title: Load gel‑dye into chip priming station
steps.instruction: Place a new chip into the chip‑priming station, add 9 µL of the gel‑dye mix into the well marked G (black circle).

steps.title: Prime chip – plunger operation
steps.instruction: Depress the plunger for exactly 30 s: pull back to the 1 mL mark, close the station, listen for the latch click, press down until the flange locks, wait 30 s, release by squeezing the syringe clip lever, wait 5 s, watch the plunger rise to ~0.7 mL, then slowly pull the flange back to the 1 mL mark at ~0.05 mL / s. If the plunger does not rise above 0.3 mL, the gasket may be leaking; prime a new chip.

steps.title: Load remaining gel‑dye wells
steps.instruction: Open the chip‑priming station and pipette 9 µL of gel‑dye mix into each of the other two wells marked G.

steps.title: Add conditioning solution
steps.instruction: Add 9 µL of RNA conditioning solution into the well marked CS.

steps.title: Add RNA marker
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL RNA marker to all 11 sample wells and to the ladder well.

steps.title: Add RNA ladder
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL RNA ladder to the well marked for the ladder.

steps.title: Load samples onto chip
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL diluted RNA sample to each sample well; add 1 µL RNA marker to each unused sample well.

steps.title: Run Bioanalyzer chip
steps.instruction: Insert the chip at an angle into the instrument, press it against the spring‑loaded latch, lower the back end until level, press start to vortex for 1 min at 2400 rpm (max speed), then start the instrument. The instrument will run a preparation phase, then analyze each well, displaying electropherograms and progress bars.

steps.title: Export Bioanalyzer data
steps.instruction: When the run finishes, export the data as .bmp images of individual electropherograms, .csv files of fluorescence values over time, .cdf, .pdf, and .xad files.

steps.title: Clean instrument after run
steps.instruction: Remove the chip, fill the electrode‑cleaning chip with 350 µL nuclease‑free water, close the lid and soak the electrodes for 5 min, remove the cleaning chip, replace the dedicated RNA cartridge with a DNA/protein cartridge, store the cartridge in a sealed box with electrodes facing upwards, and shut the instrument down.
